html:
SMTO-PRL-0001 — This setting can't change while work is still running

GUID: 6d1711c5-0b8d-4860-a286-fee68f7bfe47
Slug: activity-settings-busy
Domain: PRL · Subsystem: prl

What happened

  • You tried to change how this task handles background or dependent steps, but some of those steps are still running or waiting. SMTO kept the old setting.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Activities section under this task in the conversation and see which steps are still running or waiting. These steps rely on the setting you're changing, so SMTO won't switch it while they're active.
  2. Wait for them to finish, or select Stop next to any step you no longer need. Once nothing depends on the setting, SMTO allows the change.
  3. Open Agent Checks, choose This run, and check whether the setting already shows your new value before you change it again. This confirms whether your change was saved, so you don't apply it twice.
  4. To change the default for future tasks instead, use Settings › Operate › Asynchronous task execution. That setting applies to new tasks and doesn't affect steps already running.

What success looks like

  • In Agent Checks for this run, the setting shows your new value and no error appears.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again: reopen Agent Checks for this run and look at the setting. If it still won't change, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't stop steps whose results you still need.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run-scope settings update was rejected because background activities are still running, or because turning off dependency-aware scheduling would strand pending, running or waiting dependency activities.

What this means

  • A settings update finds active background activities, or disabling dependency scheduling finds pending/running/waiting dependency activities that still need it. Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.

Why this can happen

  • A settings update finds active background activities, or disabling dependency scheduling finds pending/running/waiting dependency activities that still need it.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact policy change and retained activity states; waiting work can block disabling even without a running process.

How to fix it

  • In the run's Activities list, let the background or dependency activities finish or stop them with their Stop controls, then re-read the run's current policy and policy_revision before reapplying the change. Earlier activity receipts are preserved; nothing is replayed.
  • Inspect and stop or join the relevant activities through their supported controls before changing the scheduler configuration. Preserve their receipts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Relevant activities settle through supported controls and the intended settings change is admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
